congenital.outcome: Generally favorable after surgical repair unless associated with syndromic anomalies

clinical_presentation: Ono’s sign: coughing worsens with swallowing
Weight loss due to fear of eating

diagnostic_approaches.notes: Gastrografin preferred; barium avoided due to risk of pulmonary edema
Provides etiologic/anatomic information; less sensitive than esophagram
Localizes and characterizes fistula; allows therapeutic intervention; methylene blue or autofluorescence can aid detection

initial_supportive: Nil per os (NPO) / strict oral intake restriction
Advance airway cuff distal to fistula if intubated
benign: Surgical repair (direct suture, flap interposition, esophageal bypass)
Sealants (fibrin glue, cyanoacrylate, platelet-rich fibrin matrix, 2-OCA) for <5 mm fistulas
Endoscopic options if surgery not feasible
malignant: Goal: palliation of symptoms, QoL improvement

stenting.esophageal: Preferred if mid/distal esophagus and no airway compromise
stenting.airway: Indicated if airway compromised or esophageal stent not tolerated
stenting.dual: Used if esophageal stenting insufficient or causes airway compression; airway stent deployed first

other_therapeutics: Tissue sealants (fibrin glue, cyanoacrylate, platelet-rich fibrin matrix, 2-OCA)
Occlusive devices (vascular plugs, silicone rings, septal buttons, decellularized matrix, PGA sheets)
EVAC (sponge with NG suction, changed every 3–5 days)
Mucosal de-epithelialization (APC, laser, electrocautery, TCA, brush)

benign.>5 mm, not surgical candidate: Airway or esophageal stent based on defect location

malignant.failed_dual: Reassess goals of care; consider comfort measures

prognosis.benign: Better outcomes with surgery; reversible if managed early
prognosis.malignant: Poorer prognosis; right mainstem fistulas, sepsis, and ventilator dependence predict worse outcomes
prognosis.palliative: Stenting improves dysphagia, dyspnea, QoL; survival benefit uncertain

points: Aerodigestive fistulas cause high morbidity/mortality and need prompt multidisciplinary management.
Benign: surgery with curative intent when feasible.
Novel therapies (EVAC, sealants, stem cells) provide adjunctive or salvage options.
QoL improvement is often achievable even without cure.
